theory.title: Both, either, neither and none
theory.explanation: Use both to refer to two things together, either to mean one or the other, neither to mean not one and not the other, and none to refer to not any of a group. Use of before a noun or pronoun: neither of my friends.
theory.tip: Both = los dos; either = cualquiera de los dos; neither = ninguno de los dos; none = ninguno del grupo.

content.passage: The health centre offers two activities each evening. Both yoga and swimming are available, and either class can help people become more active. Neither of the sessions is designed only for experts, so beginners are welcome. None of the activities requires expensive equipment. The centre also offers advice about sleep and healthy eating. Visitors can choose either a morning or an evening appointment.

items.modelAnswer: I think looking after your health is about building realistic habits and making balanced choices. I try to stay active, drink enough water and get regular sleep. When I feel stressed, I take a break or go for a walk. It is important to follow medical advice and ask questions when something is unclear. Small changes can make a big difference over time, especially when people keep practising them.

content.audioTranscript: A: Have you got your appointment tomorrow? B: Yes, I want to talk about my daily routine. A: Are you doing enough exercise? B: I'm trying to. The doctor gave me some useful advice. A: What did they suggest? B: Drinking more water and getting enough sleep. A: Do you need any medicine? B: No, but I need to rest during my recovery. A: I hope you feel better by tomorrow.
